metadata.description: Official state government sources for employer labor law compliance. Reformatted to match batch crawler schema.

jurisdictions.agency: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development
jurisdictions.notes: Alaska has state minimum wage ($11.91/hr as of 2024). Wage and Hour pamphlets (PAM-100) are key employer resources.
Alabama follows federal FLSA for minimum wage. No state minimum wage law. Workers Comp and Child Labor are primary state-level concerns.

jurisdictions.agency: Arkansas Department of Labor and Licensing (ADLL)
jurisdictions.notes: Arkansas has state minimum wage ($11.00/hr as of 2024). Labor Standards division handles wage/hour and child labor.
Arizona has Prop 206 (Fair Wages and Healthy Families Act) covering minimum wage and earned paid sick time. ICA is the primary regulatory body.
California has the most comprehensive state labor laws. DIR/DLSE handles enforcement. EDD handles UI/SDI/PFL. Multiple industry-specific wage orders apply.

jurisdictions.agency: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment (CDLE)
jurisdictions.notes: Colorado has robust worker protections. COMPS Order #39 covers overtime and meal/rest breaks. HFWA (Healthy Families & Workplaces Act) mandates paid sick leave. FAMLI program provides paid family and medical leave insurance (benefits started Jan 2024). State minimum wage is $14.42/hr (2024).

Connecticut has CT Paid Leave program (separate authority from CTDOL). CHRO (Commission on Human Rights and Opportunities) handles discrimination. State minimum wage is $15.69/hr (2024). Mandatory paid sick leave for employers with 50+ employees.
Delaware has Healthy Delaware Families Act (paid family leave) phasing in 2025-2026. State minimum wage is $13.25/hr (2024). Office of Anti-Discrimination handles EEO matters.

Florida follows federal law for most labor standards. State minimum wage is $13.00/hr (2024), increasing $1/year until $15/hr in 2026 per Amendment 2 (2020). No state income tax. Workers Comp is through CFO/DFS. Renamed from DEO to Dept of Commerce in 2023.

Georgia has state minimum wage of $5.15/hr but federal FLSA ($7.25/hr) applies to most employers. State Board of Workers' Compensation (SBWC) is separate agency. Georgia is an at-will employment state with limited state-level labor protections beyond federal requirements.

jurisdictions.agency: Hawaii Department of Labor and Industrial Relations
jurisdictions.notes: Hawaii has Temporary Disability Insurance (TDI) requirement.
Iowa has IOSH (Iowa OSHA).
Idaho follows federal minimum wage. Workers' Comp through Industrial Commission.
Illinois Paid Leave for All Workers Act effective 2024.
Indiana has IOSHA (Indiana OSHA).
Kansas follows federal minimum wage.
Kentucky has KY OSH program.
Louisiana has no state minimum wage; federal FLSA applies.

jurisdictions.agency: Massachusetts Executive Office of Labor and Workforce Development
jurisdictions.notes: Massachusetts PFML is one of the most comprehensive in the US.
Maryland FAMLI program launching 2026.
Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave begins 2026.

jurisdictions.agency: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity
jurisdictions.notes: Michigan has MIOSHA and Paid Medical Leave Act.

jurisdictions.agency: Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry
jurisdictions.notes: Minnesota Paid Leave begins 2026. Has earned sick and safe time.

jurisdictions.agency: Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations
jurisdictions.notes: Missouri minimum wage is indexed to CPI.
Mississippi has no state minimum wage; federal FLSA applies.

jurisdictions.agency: Montana Department of Labor and Industry
jurisdictions.notes: Montana minimum wage is indexed to CPI.
North Carolina follows federal minimum wage. Has OSH Division.

jurisdictions.agency: North Dakota Department of Labor and Human Rights
jurisdictions.notes: North Dakota follows federal minimum wage.
Nebraska voters approved minimum wage increases through 2026.
New Hampshire follows federal minimum wage.

jurisdictions.agency: New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development
jurisdictions.notes: New Jersey has comprehensive Family Leave Insurance and Earned Sick Leave.

jurisdictions.agency: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions
jurisdictions.notes: New Mexico Healthy Workplaces Act (paid sick leave) effective 2022.

jurisdictions.agency: Nevada Office of the Labor Commissioner
jurisdictions.notes: Nevada has two-tier minimum wage based on health benefits. Paid leave law effective 2020. Daily overtime (8hrs) covered in Labor Commissioner FAQ.

jurisdictions.agency: New York State Department of Labor
jurisdictions.notes: New York has robust Paid Family Leave and multiple minimum wage tiers (NYC, Long Island, Westchester vs rest of state).

jurisdictions.agency: Ohio Department of Commerce - Division of Industrial Compliance
jurisdictions.notes: Ohio minimum wage is indexed to CPI. BWC handles workers' comp.
Oklahoma follows federal minimum wage.

jurisdictions.agency: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries
jurisdictions.notes: Oregon has three-tier minimum wage (Portland Metro, Standard, Nonurban). Paid Leave Oregon began 2023.

jurisdictions.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry
jurisdictions.notes: Pennsylvania follows federal minimum wage.

jurisdictions.agency: Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training
jurisdictions.notes: Rhode Island has TDI/TCI (Temporary Caregiver Insurance) and Healthy and Safe Families Act.

jurisdictions.agency: South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation
jurisdictions.notes: South Carolina has no state minimum wage; federal FLSA applies. Has SC OSHA.

jurisdictions.agency: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation
jurisdictions.notes: South Dakota minimum wage is indexed to CPI.

jurisdictions.agency: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development
jurisdictions.notes: Tennessee has no state minimum wage; federal FLSA applies. Has TOSHA.
Texas follows federal minimum wage ($7.25/hr). TWC handles most labor law enforcement. Workers Comp is through TDI (separate agency). Texas is an at-will employment state.
Utah follows federal minimum wage. Has Utah OSHA.

jurisdictions.agency: Virginia Department of Labor and Industry
jurisdictions.notes: Virginia has VOSH (Virginia OSH). Minimum wage increases scheduled.
Vermont has Earned Sick Time law. Minimum wage indexed to CPI.

jurisdictions.agency: Washington State Department of Labor and Industries
jurisdictions.notes: Washington has comprehensive Paid Family & Medical Leave (PFML) and highest state minimum wage.
Wisconsin follows federal minimum wage.
West Virginia minimum wage is $8.75/hr.
Wyoming minimum wage is $5.15/hr but federal FLSA applies to most employers.

jurisdictions.agency: U.S. Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Division
jurisdictions.notes: Federal FLSA baseline. Covers minimum wage ($7.25/hr), overtime (40 hrs/week), child labor, and recordkeeping.
